candidates.audience: People planning roofing work on properties confirmed within City of Chicago jurisdiction
candidates.offer: Use city building-permit guidance and Illinois licensing records to compare a roofing project scope. No lead collection or booking.
candidates.headline: Chicago reroofing: permits, licensing and scope checks
candidates.subhead: Five checks to make before hiring a roofer, backed by the City of Chicago and Illinois licensing guidance.
candidates.summary: A citywide research checklist for properties under Chicago jurisdiction. Check the actual address and project before relying on permit rules. no contractor referral or sale is offered.

local_facts.statement: Chicago lists roof repair covering up to 25% of roof area, roof recovery over one existing covering layer, and nonstructural roof replacement among work potentially eligible for its Express Permit Program. Extra layers or structural repairs can require architect or engineer documentation. Check all stated limits for the specific project.
local_facts.source_ref: Chicago Department of Buildings: Express Permit eligibility, reroofing

local_facts.statement: The City of Chicago explains that permits are generally needed for most construction and repair work. Check the precise project and property circumstances against the current city guidance.
local_facts.source_ref: City of Chicago: Building Permit Application Instructions

local_facts.statement: Chicago's permit-application status service offers limited public application information by property address. It says records for applications older than 36 months may not appear.
local_facts.source_ref: City of Chicago: Building Permit Application Status Help

local_facts.statement: Chicago's reroofing permit guidance rules out work by someone without a valid Illinois Roofing Contractor license. The Illinois professional licensing authority provides a lookup to verify an individual or business license.
The Census Bureau's ZIP Code Tabulation Areas are generalized approximations of USPS delivery ZIP codes. A ZIP or ZCTA alone does not establish which municipality's permit rules apply to a property.
local_facts.source_ref: US Census Bureau: ZIP Code Tabulation Areas

research_steps: Confirm the property is within City of Chicago jurisdiction using its actual street address. ZIP codes and census ZCTAs alone do not establish jurisdiction.

Identify the proposed scope. Chicago lists repairs up to 25% of roof area, recovery over one existing covering layer, and nonstructural replacement among possible Express Permit projects. Confirm extra roof layers, structural work and insulation requirements against official eligibility rules.
Get the contractor's registered business name and Illinois roofing license details, then check the official state licensing lookup rather than relying on an advertisement.
Look up the property address in Chicago's permit application status service, remembering that information may be limited and applications older than 36 months may be absent.
Compare written bids for material specifications, existing layers, structural work, insulation, waste removal, warranties and which party will secure required permits.
